subject: Remote-site deployment: evidence scope & limited audit proposal
messages:
From: Anna Morales <anna.morales@medtechco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: remote-site deployment terms and evidence request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood’s private deployment option. Our legal/procurement team has a few open items before we can finalize the Order Form and MSA addendum for the on-prem/VPC deployment. I’m attaching our standard evidence & audit request so you can review. High-level asks: 

- Clarify license scope for on-prem: can customer run sub-processes for inference (batch imports) and what constitutes "usage" vs. "deployment" for license metrics.
- Custody & key management: we prefer a custody attestation and an optional escrow-like mechanism if keys are required for restore.
- Audit window: ability for a third-party auditor to validate certain controls at customer premises or via remote evidence collection once per 12 months.
- Source-code/escrow: our counsel sometimes asks for escrow-escrow alternatives (verifiable runbooks, image hashes) instead of full source-code escrow.

Can you confirm what Redwood typically provides for customers on this footprint and whether you can accept a limited audit clause (time-boxed, scope-limited to deployment/environment controls) instead of open audit rights? We’d also like an updated Order Form reflecting the dedicated deployment SKU and pricing once legal terms are in alignment.

Attached: MedTech_Evidence_Request_20270219.pdf (evidence matrix, sample attestation language)

If useful I can loop in our procurement lead (Alan Chen) — he handles final order form details. Would you and your legal rep be available for a 30-minute sync next week?

Thanks,
Anna Morales
Sr. Counsel, MedTech Solutions
anna.morales@medtechco.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Morales <anna.morales@medtechco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: remote-site deployment terms and evidence request

Hi Anna — appreciate the clear matrix. Looping in our SE (Marcus) and legal (Laura) so we can respond precisely. Quick answers and next steps from our side: 

- License scope: Redwood’s Private/On‑Prem license is based on deployed instances (per-host SKU) + usage-based inference tokens. For batch imports run purely inside customer environment, the licensing is covered by the deployed-instance SKU; we’ll put explicit examples in the draft clause.

- Keys & custody: we don’t require customer keys for runtime; however customers who want HSM/KMS integrations can supply keys and we’ll offer an attestation template. For disaster recovery, we can provide a dual-path approach: (a) attestation + image hashes retained with a named custodian; or (b) a narrow escrow via a third-party custodian under predefined triggers (only used for disaster recovery).

- Audits: we’re open to a single annual, scoped audit (30 business days advance notice) that’s limited to deployment/configuration and evidence already produced for SOC2/SecOps. No access to source code — we can provide runtime artifacts, checksums, and a secure remote session for verification instead of on-site access unless strictly required.

Action items: Laura will propose redline language for the MSA addendum and Order Form. Marcus will assemble the technical evidence bundle (runbooks, image hashes, restore playbook). I’ll coordinate a 30-minute call; proposed slots: Tue 2/23 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed 2/24 09:00-09:30 PT.

Sending draft redlines and a short evidence matrix now (attached).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
+1 (650) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Draft: remote-site deployment terms and evidence request

Hi Anna — thanks for the matrix. I reviewed your items and drafted a set of proposed MSA addendum redlines and an Order Form clause that reflect Redwood’s production and security posture but also address your concerns. Key points in the proposed language (see attached redline pdf):

1) License & usage definition: add an explicit definition of "Deployed Instance" (host-based) and a non-exhaustive examples section clarifying batch imports and offline scoring are covered by deployed-instance usage; token-based billing reserved for Redwood-managed execution.

2) Custody & escrow alternative: proposed compromise clause: 
   - Redwood will provide a signed custody attestation annually (format in attachment).
   - For DR scenarios, customer may request limited release of artifacts (image hashes, signed binaries) held by a neutral third-party custodian upon mutually agreed trigger events; procedure and release criteria are enumerated.

3) Audit right (narrow): allow one annual third-party audit limited to config and deployment artifacts; scope excludes source code and internal proprietary tooling. Audit execution options: remote evidence package + short remote session (preferred) or on-site only if specific conditions met (severity, unresolved issues).

4) Evidence package & retention: Redwood will provide the runbook, image hashes, restore checklist, and SOC2 summary for the deployed version. We propose a 12-month retention window for evidence relevant to the deployed release.

Next steps I recommend:
- Marcus: attach the technical evidence package (runbook, image hashes).
- Priyom: review pricing impact for the limited custodian option and add a short Order Form amendment.
- Kimberly: confirm which slot works for the 30-min sync.

If these redlines look acceptable for you, we can convert the Order Form and issue a DocuSign envelope for signature post-call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
